newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco devotes $9.6 mln to local election campaign.
newsitem.headline: Morocco devotes $9.6 mln to local election campaign.

text.p: Morocco has devoted 90 million dirhams ($9.6 million) to finance political parties campaigning for local council election due on June 13, an interior ministry official said on Saturday.
A dozen political parties, including five opposition groups, announced their decision to stand for communal elections, the official said.
"The government decided to devote 90 million dirhams as financial support to political parties which will participate to communal elections," he added.
More than 102,000 candidates, of which nearly 40,000 belong to the opposition, will compete for 24,253 seats the poll.
Campaigning for the elections, which started on May 29, will end on June 12.
According to the interior ministry, 14,447 candidates are standing as independents. The remainder come from 12 political parties.
Initially, 13 political parties were expected to stand but the centre-right Mouvement Populaire Democratique et Constitutionnel (MPDC) withdrew its candidacy at the last minute, officials said.
The old-guard opposition Istiqlal party, was the only political group to cover more than 50 percent of the country's constituencies, including the disputed Western Sahara, the ministry said.
Local elections are the first of a series which will be capped by a parliamentary poll in September, with a new bicameral parliament being inaugurated by King Hassan on the second Friday of October.
Under the new constitution, the Lower House of parliament will be directly elected through universal suffrage.
Local councils will elect around 80 percent of the members of the new Upper House of Parliament being set up under constitutional reforms approved last September.
The new house will have power to vote a no-confidence motion in the government and could topple it.
